deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The surrounding pages treat an unbranched cyclic covering of a Riemann surface T of genus p. The cut a_rho is continued through the lambda sheets, giving a lambda-sheeted surface. On the cover the cuts a_nu, b_nu with nu<rho are repeated lambda times (a_nu^alpha, b_nu^alpha), while a_rho and b_rho are single. The page has three parts.

(A) lambda = 3, rho = varrho = exp(2 pi i/3).

A1. The normal integrals. For each nu<rho, w_nu, w'_nu, w''_nu are the normal integrals of the cover with modulus pi i at the cut a_nu on sheet 0, 1, 2 respectively. Implicitly (my statement):
- u_nu = w+w'+w'' (the lift of the base integral),
- v_nu = w + varrho w' + varrho^2 w'',
- v'_nu = w + varrho^2 w' + varrho w''.
The top line is the inversion of this discrete Fourier transform: w = (u+v+v')/3, w' = (u+varrho^2 v+varrho v')/3, w'' = (u+varrho v+varrho^2 v')/3.

A2. Moduli at the b-cuts. The modulus of w_nu at b_mu (same sheet) is (a_{mu,nu}+b_{mu,nu}+b_{nu,mu})/3. By the deck symmetry, the modulus of w^alpha at b^beta depends only on beta-alpha, and the three possible values are (a + varrho^j b_{mu,nu} + varrho^{-j} b_{nu,mu})/3. Each w at b_rho has modulus a_{nu,rho}.

A3. General period. Riemann writes the general period of w, w', w'' for a closed path crossing a^alpha_mu g times and b^beta_mu h times: g_nu pi i + (1/3) Sum[h_mu(...) + h'_mu(...) + h''_mu(...)] + h_rho a_{nu,rho}. The three bracket patterns are cyclically permuted between w, w', w''. The first formula line (subscript rho) is the analogous period of the lifted u_rho: g_rho pi i + Sum(h+h'+h'')a_{mu,rho} + 3 h_rho a_{rho,rho}.

A4. Periods of u, v, v'. Summing gives the period of u_nu: (g+g'+g'') pi i + Sum(h+h'+h'')a_{mu,nu} + 3 h_rho a_{nu,rho}. Here g'_rho = g''_rho = 0 because there is only one a_rho cut. Weighting with 1, varrho, varrho^2 gives:
- v_nu: pi i (g+g' varrho+g'' varrho^2) + Sum b_{mu,nu}(h+h' varrho+h'' varrho^2);
- v'_nu: the same with varrho replaced by varrho^2 and b_{mu,nu} replaced by b_{nu,mu}.
The a-parts cancel because 1+varrho+varrho^2 = 0, and so does the b_rho modulus. So v, v' are 'Prym-type' integrals: their periods are pi i times Eisenstein integers and b-matrix times Eisenstein integers, with v' carrying the conjugate integers and the transposed matrix.

A5. The theta series. Riemann defines theta = Sum exp(2 Sum b_{mu,nu} n'_mu n_nu + 2 Sum(v_nu n_nu + v'_nu n'_nu)). For convergence (my inference, confirmed by the next page, where n^kappa = Sum m^alpha alpha^{-alpha g^kappa}), the n_nu must be Eisenstein integers and n'_nu their conjugates. The quadratic form is then Hermitian; with independent integers n, n' it would be indefinite.

A6. Properties stated. Under this reading:
- (i) theta(varrho v, varrho^2 v') = theta(varrho^2 v, varrho v') (= theta(v,v')): substitute n -> unit*n.
- (ii) theta(v+pi i, v'+pi i) = theta: n + conj(n) is an ordinary integer.
- (iii) theta(-v,-v') = theta.
- (iv) Quasi-periodicity: shifting n_iota and n'_iota by 1 adds 2 Sum b_{mu,iota} n'_mu + 2 Sum b_{iota,nu} n_nu + 2 b_{iota,iota} + 2(v_iota+v'_iota), the increment written on the right. Hence theta(v,v') = theta(v_nu + b_{iota,nu}, v'_mu + b_{mu,iota}) exp(2(v_iota+v'_iota) + 2 b_{iota,iota}).

(B) Period table for a genus-2 base with rho = 2 and general odd lambda.
- u_1, u_2 have periods (pi i, 0, a11, a12) and (0, pi i, a21, a22).
- The lifts w_1..w_lambda of u_1 have pi i at their own a-cut and moduli c_0, c_1, ..., c_{lambda-1} (cyclically shifted) at the lambda b_1-cuts, and a_{1,2} at b_2.
- u_2 has modulus a_{1,2} at each b_1-cut and lambda a_{2,2} at b_2.

(C) General lambda = 2mu+1, alpha a primitive lambda-th root of unity, q a primitive root mod lambda.
- Sum_nu w_nu = u_1.
- v_k = Sum_nu w_nu alpha^{nu q^k}.
- Using c_beta = c_{-beta}, the b_1^0-modulus of v_k is b_k = c_0 + c_1(alpha^{q^k}+alpha^{-q^k}) + ... + c_mu(alpha^{mu q^k}+alpha^{-mu q^k}).
- Since q^mu = -1 mod lambda, b_k = b_{k+mu}.
- theta = Sum exp(Sum_k b_k n_k n_{k+mu} + n_k v_k + n_{k+mu} v_{k+mu}), with n_k the Galois conjugates of a cyclotomic integer, so that n_{k+mu} = conj(n_k).

This is a Hermitian theta function over Z[alpha] for the (lambda-1)-dimensional 'Prym' part of the Jacobian of the cyclic cover.
errors: As written, theta = Sum exp(2 Sum b n'_mu n_nu + ...) with n, n' independent rational integers would diverge: a quadratic form with only an off-diagonal block is indefinite. The page silently requires n_nu in Z[varrho] and n'_nu = conj(n_nu). This is only made explicit on the next page.
The statement theta(v varrho, v' varrho^2) = theta(v varrho^2, v' varrho) is partly struck out. It is true only under the Eisenstein-integer reading, not for an ordinary 2(p-1)-variable theta series.

The index labels in theta(v_iota + b_{nu,iota}, v'_iota + b_{iota,nu}) are loose. Read literally, the order is transposed relative to the computation: component nu of v should be shifted by b_{iota,nu}, and component mu of v' by b_{mu,iota}. The exponential factor exp(2(v_iota+v'_iota)+2b_{iota,iota}) and the side on which it stands are correct.
In the w' line the last term is written h_mu a_{nu,rho}; it should be h_rho a_{nu,rho}. This is a slip of the pen.
The first period line has subscript rho, i.e. it gives the period of u_rho. It is mislabelled w_nu in the transcription, and its a_{mu,rho}/a_{rho,rho} indices are consistent only with u_rho.

results.what: Discrete-Fourier (character) decomposition of the normal integrals of an unbranched cyclic triple (and lambda-fold) cover into the lifted base integrals u and eigen-integrals v, v' with periods in Z[varrho]-lattices
results.modern_name: Isogeny decomposition Jac(C~) ~ Jac(C) x Prym(C~/C) for cyclic etale covers; eigenspace decomposition of differentials under the deck group
results.usually_credited_to: Prym (1866-69, double covers, under Riemann's influence); Wirtinger (1895, Untersuchungen ueber Thetafunctionen) for general Prym varieties; Mumford (1974) for the modern theory

results.what: Period formulas for v_nu, v'_nu: pi i(g+g' varrho+g'' varrho^2) + Sum b_{mu,nu}(h+h' varrho+h'' varrho^2), with v' carrying the conjugate integers and the transposed matrix
results.modern_name: Period lattice of the Prym variety as a Z[zeta]-module (Hermitian / CM-type structure)
results.usually_credited_to: Wirtinger 1895; later Fay (1973) for cyclic covers

results.what: Theta series summed over Eisenstein (resp. cyclotomic) integers with Hermitian form Sum b_{mu,nu} conj(n_mu) n_nu; invariance under units, under v -> v+pi i, and quasi-periodicity
results.modern_name: Hermitian theta function on a lattice over Z[zeta_lambda] (Prym theta of a cyclic cover)
results.usually_credited_to: Wirtinger (1895); Hermitian theta functions in general to later authors (e.g. Cohn, Shimura)

results.what: b_k = Sum c_beta alpha^{beta q^k} with b_k = b_{k+mu}, using a primitive root q with q^mu = -1 mod lambda (Gaussian-period style indexing)
results.modern_name: Galois conjugates over Q(zeta_lambda) indexed by a primitive root; Fourier transform on Z/lambda
Inverse discrete Fourier transform on Z/3

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann's involvement with Prym's double covers is known, so the general idea of decomposing the theta function of an unbranched cover is not unexpected from him. A worked treatment of cyclic covers of odd prime degree, with a Hermitian theta series over Eisenstein/cyclotomic integers for the Prym part, anticipates material usually associated with Wirtinger (1895) and later work on cyclic covers. That makes it a notable unpublished detail. Whether these Nachlass sheets have already been discussed in the literature is unclear, so I stay conservative.

transcription_corrections: The first period line reads 'w_rho (or u_rho) = g_rho pi i + Sum(h_mu+h'_mu+h''_mu) a_{mu,rho} + 3 h_rho a_{rho,rho}', not 'w_nu = ...'.
The line under the first contains the separate expression (1/3)(a_{mu,nu}+b_{mu,nu}+b_{nu,mu}), the modulus of w_nu at b_mu.
In the w'_nu line the final term is written 'h_mu a_{nu,rho}' in the manuscript (Riemann's slip for h_rho a_{nu,rho}).
The symmetry line is partly struck out; it reads approximately theta(v_iota varrho, v'_iota varrho^2) [struck: ...theta(v_iota, v'_iota)] = theta(v_iota varrho^2, v'_iota varrho).

'Sum_varrho w_nu varrho^{nu k} = v_k' should be read Sum_nu w_nu alpha^{nu q^k} = v_k, and 'c_1(a^{q^k}+a^{-q^k})' should be c_1(alpha^{q^k}+alpha^{-q^k}). The base letter is the root of unity alpha with exponent q^k, q a primitive root.
The marginal note at the right of the last formula line reads 'b_k = b_{k+mu}'.

Table: the w_1 row has 'pi i 0 ... a_1 a_2 | b_1^{(lambda)} b_2'; subsequent rows list c_0, c_1, ..., c_{lambda-1} (cyclically shifted) and a_{1,2}; the u_2 row ends with 'a_{1,2} ... lambda a_{2,2}'.
Final line: theta = Sum e^{Sum b_k n_k n_{k+mu} + n_k v_k + n_{k+mu} v_{k+mu}}.
